The objective of this grant will be to support the government.s efforts in improving efficiency and quality of PFM by implementing a part of the Action Plan, namely capacity building of SAI. The aim of the proposal will be obtained through; (1) assessment of capacity, drafting of strategy, and writing of audit & training manuals, (2) training, and (3) strengthening of archive and IT systems. Component 1: Assessment of capacity, drafting of strategy, and writing of audit & training manuals Prior to the training component, an assessment of the capacity of the SAI staff will be carried out in order to review the need and areas for training. Based of the assessment, a strategy for medium-term capacity building including the design of the training modules will be developed. The long term impact of this grant will be secured through the writing of audit manuals including ethics guidelines and training manuals. The studies proposed under this component will be done by two consultants - 1 international and 1 local consultant. Some equipment (2 laptop computers, and 1 printer) will be required in order for the consultants to carry out their assignments. Component 2: Training Based on the capacity assessment of SAI staff and the strategy for medium-term capacity building, the objective of this grant component will be to train the magistrates and experts of the SAI. The grant will finance the training of 50 magistrates and staff in the areas identified in the assessment. The Government has suggested the following training areas; (1) auditing of state accounts, (2) auditing of local authorities, (3) auditing of budget execution, (4) auditing of public sector and state-owned enterprises, and (5) control sanctions: Gestion de fait (management by a person who does not effectively possess the title of accountant but has acted as such). The training will be provided by 1 international consultant and 1 local consultant (to leave behind national capacity). The consultants will require some equipment (1 laptop computer, and 1 PowerPoint projector) to carry out the training sessions. Component 3: Strengthening of archive and IT systems In addition to the lack of training, the capacity of SAI remains low in two areas; (1) archive system, and (2) IT system. At present, the SAI does not have the capacity to develop an effective filing system and the grant will therefore finance the recruitment of 2 local consultants to organize the archive system. With the creation of a website, the SAI will be able to reach a much wider audience and disseminate information on a regular basis. The grant will finance the design and creation of a website including establishment of a local area network (LAN). Since the SAI has a limited number of computers available, the procurement of 8 computers will be covered by the grant. The 8 computers will allow SAI staff to profit from the creation of the website and the establishment of the LAN. The outcome of this grant will be improvement of the technical capacity of SAI staff. The provided training will strengthen the SAI and elevate the quality of magistrates to a desirable level. The long term impact of this grant will be secured through the writing of audit and training manuals. The Development Objective of the Grant is to assist the Supreme Audit Institution (Cours des Comptes) in its efforts to improve efficiency and quality of the public financial management (PFM) systems by strengthening its capacity building through the following activities : 1. Assessment of capacity, drafting of strategy and writing of audit and training Manual. 2. Improvement of the technical capacity of SAI staff. 3. Strenghtening of Archive and Information Technology System.

Project Objectives and Description. The objective of the Project is to establish acceptable audit practices in line with international standards and improve quality of services provided by the accountancy profession in Senegal. The Project consists of the following parts: Part A: Adapting the Local Audit Standards to ISA and General Professional Guidelines and Ethical Code of IFAC Provide support to Order National des Experts Comptables et Comptables Agréés (ONECCA) to adapt the auditing standards of International Standards on Auditing (ISA) and general professional guidelines and ethical code of International Federation of Accountants (IFAC) by: (a) reviewing the existing national standards and code of ethics in line with ISA and IFAC's code of ethics; (b) disseminating and promoting the standards and; (c) capacity building of ONECCA members on ISA and International Financing Reporting Standards (IFRS). all of the above through the provision of technical advisory services, goods, and training and workshops. Part B: Establishment of Audit Quality Review Schemes Provide support in establishing an Audit Quality Review (AQR) scheme for adherence with IFAC standards through: (a) drafting of curriculum; (b) capacity building of ONECCA members for peer review practice of audit control system; and (c) printing and dissemination of AQR manual and guidelines. all of the above through provision of technical advisory services, goods, and training and workshops. Part C: Enhancing the Capacity of Local Training Institutions Provide support to: (a) at least three local training institutions to be accredited with Diplome d'Expertise Comptable et Financiere (DECOFI) and to enable these institutions to deliver DECOFI services through establishment of a local area network system, website, and database for membership information; and (b) review the curricula of Le Conseil d'Administration du Centre Africain D'Etudes Supérieures (CESAG) to make the accounting and auditing degree program more accessible. all of the above through the provision of technical advisory services, goods, and training. The overall objective of the IDF grant is to establish acceptable audit practices in line with international standards and improve quality of services provided by the Accountancy profession in Senegal.

title.narrative: Senegal Nutrition Strengthening Operational Evaluation in Program implementation

description.narrative: "The objective of this proposal is to strengthen the use of operational evaluation to more quickly adjust interventions for greater impact and to adopt results based approaches to more quickly scale up successful interventions. The proposed IDF is designed to finance 3 types of activities: 1) Operational research/evaluation; 2) strengthening the capacity at various levels to report in real time on the condition of mothers and children in each of the communities, and 3) to accelerate implementation and scale up of successful interventions based on the results of the operations research and community assessments. 1. Operational research/evaluation is designed to answer questions related to the effectiveness and efficiency of various interventions. Given that within each community a number of interventions are taking place simultaneously, one of the purposes of this research or evaluation is to answer questions related a. Which combination of interventions is having the greatest impact? b. What is the value added of breast feeding exclusively for the first six months, relative to other interventions? c. How effective is the cash transfer program being considered to those chronically malnourished? d. What type of intervention would be best in a particular community given their nutritional status? More vitamin fortification or iodized salt, or mosquito bed nets? e. What are the most cost effective interventions given specific conditions? 2. Strengthening the capacity at the community and regional level to report on and take action based on regular assessments of their communities' nutritional status. a. Regular standardized reports on the health and nutritional status of mothers and children in each community. b. The ability to generate a minimal level of analysis at the community level to allow program leaders to take corrective action immediately: inventories of certain medications are low or out, the ""relais"" are not showing up on time or at all, spot checking the proper use of bed nets by mothers and children, etc. c. An effort to simplify and standardized the M&E system being generated by the community level and to disseminate this information systematically to regional and national authorities. This will allow program leaders to zero in on successful (or non-responsive) interventions and better understand why things are working or not. 3. Strengthen program implementation in new communities and/or of different interventions in existing communities. The idea is to systematically integrate the results of the operational research and community assessments into action. a. Train regional community program leaders on results based management b. Identify and train ""coaches"" to serve as training of trainers to support program leaders in strengthening their leadership and management skills c. Train program leaders to design implementation approaches that engage in learning and discovery of various types of intervention to ascertain their feasibility, scaling up potential, and cost effectiveness. The above approach builds on a strong Monitoring and Evaluation system and is designed to take it to the next level of real time analysis and rapid implementation. The PRN has an effective, lean information system from data collected monthly at the community level, which provides information on project activities, outcome indicators, and costs. This activity will continue to form the basis of SNEP's monitoring system while being adapted and improved according to strategic changes and needs. Emphasizing the importance of outcome-based monitoring, the project requires that implementing organizations conduct Knowledge, Practices and Coverage (KPC) surveys using standardized tools, sampling and data collection methods. These KPC surveys will be conducted at the beginning and end of a subproject. This information is analyzed and interpreted in relation to relevant national surveys, notably the DHS and the Multiple Indicator Cluster Surveys. Active involvement of stakeholders will be important to create ownership of the information. Therefore, community management committees periodically will discuss monthly results presented by community workers. The development objective of this grant is to: (i) strengthen two weak links in the M&E system of the PRN, namely operational research and community analysis [the current M&E system of the Programme de Renforcement de la Nutrition, Nutrition Strengthening Program (PRN)] essentially geared towards the monitoring of results of activities in the project sites but generates little important information for the documentation of best practices); and (ii) promote leadership and management capacity of actors in the PRN."

The purpose of this IDF grant is to build country capacity to assess, manage and monitor the environmental and social safeguards risks in development projects to reduce the negative externalities of large-scale infrastructure investments in the energy and transport sectors and targeted interventions in other sectors. Grant activities would include all Senegalese agencies involved in infrastructure investments, in particular the Ministry of Investment, with APIX leading the work as the grant recipient. The grant will permit APIX to determine where current safeguards capacities lie as well as identify key gaps in government capabilities regarding safeguards assessment, planning, monitoring and management within and across ministries. Grant funds will be earmarked for baseline diagnostic work as well as activities to strengthen incentives for adopting best practice with respect to safeguards processes and tools as well as provide support for skills enhancement and training among government technical staff tasked with application and oversight of investment project safeguards. The Development Objective of this grant is to strengthen the assessment, enforcement and monitoring and evaluation capacity of national safeguard practitioners in the use of Senegal's environmental and social safeguards country systems.

description.narrative: "The Government of Senegal and the communes affected by the program will jointly conduct the following activities, with the support of UN-HABITAT and FDV: 1. Development of strategic themes of the ""Senegalese Cities without Slums"" program, and reporting and validation thereof. 3. Preparation of an action plan for rendering the strategy operational (methodology, regulatory and technical tools, institutional actors and mechanisms), and the relevant reporting/validation. 4. Mobilization of financial resources needed for their implementation at the local, national, and international levels. 5. Establishment of communication and internalization mechanisms to promote involvement of local collectivities and neighborhood associations. 6. Preparation and implementation of a training program for relevant actors [government - MUAT, executing agencies (e.g., FDV), local collectivities of communes affected by the program, associations representing beneficiary populations]. 7. Exploitation and dissemination of program results."

title.narrative: Senegal Health ResultBased Financing Trust Fund

description.narrative: "The proposed USAID TF will contribute to the achievement of the PDO of the project P129472. Namely, this PDO is to increase utilization and quality of maternal, neonatal, child health and nutritional services, especially among the poorest households in targeted areas of Senegal. Given its amount, the USAID TF will focus only on 2 regions (Kolda and Kaffrine), while IDA and HRITF funding will focus on four other regions. More precisely, the PDO is expected to be achieved through the implementation of the RBF mechanism. This mechanism will incentivize facilities and their staff on the achievement of the following indicators: 1. Births (deliveries) attended by skilled health personnel; 2. Women receiving Postnatal care; 3. Number of fully immunized children (0-11 months); 4. Contraceptive prevalence rate; 5. Children 0-24 months receiving adequate weight nutritional monitoring; 6. Testing for Tuberculosis; and 7. HIV+ pregnant women under Anti Retro Viral (ARV) treatment."
